ctx.x: was losing money right and left, right and left. It cost me to play dates.

And so I told them, I'm going to send everybody home. And I'm just going to use a small group. So then I -- Witherspoon was with me then. And how I ran into Witherspoon, we did a one-nighter in Vallejo, California, after I'd came out of the service. I had Blues Bailey singing with me, but he went over to join Charlie Barnet . And so I didn't have a blues singer that night.

items.title: Jimmy Witherspoon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, FL, April 12, 1996
items.q: Then that’s where I joined Jay McShann.

ctx.x: Then that’s where I joined Jay McShann. Actually, that’s where the mess started.
Would you do it again? Who did you replace, or did he have a singer before you?

items.title: Jay McShann interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: Yes, yes, Spoon came on board later. We had a lot of fun, yes sir.

ctx.x: Yeah? No kidding. My goodness. And Jimmy Witherspoon came on board a little bit later?
Yes, yes, Spoon came on board later. We had a lot of fun, yes sir. Yeah Spoon wanted to sing the blues. Yeah, he wanted to sing the blues.
You had a big hand in his first recordings, right? “Ain’t Nobody’s Business.”
